_what: Per-shot overrides for the shot list: tags the derivation gets wrong or cannot see, and extra links.
_why: build_shots.py derives tags from each shot's own light/craft/subject prose, which covers all 565 without hand-writing 565 entries. This file is where a human disagrees. An entry's `tags` REPLACES the derived set; `addTags` appends to it; `links` are merged by URL.

_tags.when: dawn | sunrise | golden | sunset | blue hour | night | midday — what time you have to be standing there
_tags.subject: wildlife | astro | aurora | water | people | blue hour
_tags.conditions: needs clear sky | moon-dependent | truck | seasonal — the things that make a shot fail on the day

_maps: Every shot with lat/lng gets a Google Maps pin automatically, and coordinates quoted inside vantage prose become links. Shots with no coordinate get no link — never guessed from a place name.
_scope: Leg 1 (9 stops, 28 shots) reviewed by hand. The rest are derived only.

Bison breath on the caprock at first lig.why: Derivation missed 'truck' — the vantage says work from the vehicle because the herd is free-ranging and often on the road, which is a safety instruction, not a convenience. Seasonal because the breath-steam only happens while Panhandle mornings are still near freezing, and 22 Mar is the edge of that.

Near-full moon rising over Haynes Ridge.why: The whole shot exists because the moon is 99% on this stay — it is moon-dependent in the positive direction, which the rule reads as a warning. Kept, because the same flag tells you the Milky Way is off the table.

Clarity Tunnel as pure geometry.why: A 9-mile round trip on the Trailway from Monk's Crossing, on a surface riders describe as sand, clay and goatheads — the truck tag is about reaching the trailhead, not riding it. Seasonal because the bat colony is a warm-season occupant and late March is early.

Star trails over the dunefield.why: Dogs are permitted on the Dunes Overlook Trail but not in the dunefield beyond the first high ridge — worth knowing before walking out in the dark with the dog.

links.label: NPS — pets at Great Sand Dunes

The last sandhill cranes.why: 'The last' is doing real work — the Monte Vista crane migration is essentially over by early April and the stop arrives 30 Mar. This is the tightest seasonal window on the leg.
The last sandhill cranes.fix_why: The vantage named Monte Vista NWR but printed the Alamosa POI coordinate, 24.4 km due east — the wrong town, at 06:00 for a 06:48 sunrise. Now carries real lat/lng for the refuge, where it previously had none at all.

vantage.append: NOTE: this coordinate is the TRAILHEAD — the slot and the ice column are about half a mile further up the creek and ~200 ft higher.

The ice column inside Zapata Falls.fix_why: Rated "short walk" while its own caution asks for neoprene to wade a snowmelt creek, microspikes for glazed rock inside the slot, and 3.5 miles of rough washboard gravel that may still be snow-drifted. The same yardstick rates Bear's Hump a real hike. The pin was the trailhead, not the falls.

Bear Lake ice, Hallett Peak alpenglow.why: NPS bans pets from every RMNP trail, tundra and meadow. Any shot here that leaves the road is a shot the dog cannot come on, and that is a planning fact, not a footnote.

Moraine Park elk at first light, no antl.why: Roadside, so the dog can be in the truck — but the tag keeps the rule visible on the stop where it bites hardest.

Greater sage-grouse strutting at Speedwa.why: Lek display peaks late March to mid-May and the stop is 24 Apr - 1 May, so this is one of the few things at this stop that is genuinely IN season while the alpine trailheads are still snowed in. Worth flagging as the reason to set an alarm here.

fix.craft: Longest lens you own, braced on the door frame, and expect a SMALL subject. WGFD puts the lek about 400 yards south of County Road 113 and you never leave the vehicle — at ~365 m a strutting male subtends only 2-3% of the frame width even at 600mm. This is a heavily-cropped environmental frame of birds on a lek, not a frame-filling portrait. Shoot for the scene: several males, frost, low light across the sage.

Greater sage-grouse strutting at Speedwa.fix_why: The card implied a portrait the optics cannot produce at the only range the access rules allow — a pre-dawn drive on a mud-season road for a disappointment.

Fremont Lake ice-out with the range stil.why: Ice-out timing is the whole shot and it varies by weeks year to year — a condition to check on arrival, not to plan around.

fix.light: Sunset, not sunrise. From Sandy Beach the range bears NE, and late-April sunrise is at azimuth ~66-70 degrees — only 25 degrees off the camera axis, so at dawn the range front you can see is its west/south-west aspect, backlit and in shadow. The warm-lit white range over a cold blue-shadowed lake is an EVENING phenomenon from Pinedale. Same picture, opposite end of the day.

Fremont Lake ice-out with the range stil.fix_why: The card had you getting up in the dark for a colour split that happens twelve hours later.

Pronghorn on the migration bottleneck at.fix_why: The reference resolved to an archived 2012 Grand Teton news release about ranger-led SAGE-GROUSE lek trips — pasted from the other shot at this same stop. Nothing about pronghorn, the Path of the Pronghorn or Trapper's Point. Removed rather than replaced with a guess.

Shoshone Falls at peak runoff, with the.why: The review found the stated time wrong by two to three hours, so the derived tags were wrong too — they were read off the uncorrected light text. Retagged from the corrected window.

fix.light: Late afternoon, early May. The bow needs the sun behind you and below about 42 degrees altitude: from the lower terraces the falls bear roughly NE, so the sun wants to be in the S-to-W arc — about 16:00-17:30 on these dates, NOT the last two hours before sunset. Morning gives clean light on the rock but no bow.

Shoshone Falls at peak runoff, with the.fix_why: Sun geometry, from the review: on these dates the last two hours put the sun at azimuth 279-299 degrees, which places the antisolar point — where a rainbow centres — at 99-119 degrees ESE. A falls viewed to the NNW is nowhere near that arc. The shot also contradicted its own directions, telling you to walk to the far downstream (west) end of the terrace, which puts the falls to your EAST/NE. Alarm goes two to three hours earlier than the card used to say.

caution.from: Roughly a 2-hour drive each way from Twin Falls — this eats a whole day of a 2-night stop, so decide in advance.
caution.to: About 72 miles and 1 h 35 - 1 h 45 each way from Twin Falls — most of a day out of a 2-night stop, so decide in advance.

subject.to: Granite spires of the ~28-million-year-old Almo Pluton (the 2.5-billion-year-old Green Creek Complex is a separate, older unit exposed in the reserve)

Emigrant signatures at City of Rocks.fix_why: The vantage said 90 minutes and the caution said 2 hours for the same drive. The review measured it at about 72 miles, 1 h 35 - 1 h 45, so the 90-minute figure was right and the caution was inflating the cost of the shot on an already-tight 2-night stop. The 2.5-billion-year age was attached to the wrong rock.

Denali over the three-river confluence.fix_why: Pin was 3.7 km NNW out in the braided Susitna channel, not a place you walk to. Moved to the river landing at the north end of Main Street, which is what the vantage describes — and it is a pre-05:00 start with a long lens and tripod.

General Sherman's base in falling snow.fix_why: Pin was 2.1 km west, out toward Round Meadow. Moved to the General Sherman Tree. In December, navigating in snow before dawn with the main lot often closed, the wrong side of the grove is a practical problem.

Ship Creek, salmon and skyline.fix_why: Pin was on the Tony Knowles Coastal Trail, 4.6 km away — wrong creek, wrong side of downtown. Moved to the Ship Creek dam and footbridge. Facing corrected to SW: from the footbridge the downtown towers bear about 230 deg, so the old W bearing put the skyline off the left edge instead of stacked behind the fish.

Flattop at 23:00.fix_why: Longitude was transposed — .2861 instead of .6822 — dropping the pin 21.3 km into the roadless Chugach backcountry. Moved to the Glen Alps trailhead. Navigating to the old point at 21:00 for a 23:15 summit sends you to the wrong side of the range with no time to recover.

Matanuska medial moraines from the highw.fix_why: Pin was on the glacier surface itself, 17.1 km inside privately controlled guided-tour-only ice that the shot own caution says you must not walk on. Moved to the state recreation site at Glenn Highway MP 101, which is the free public wayside the shot is actually about.

subject.from: Early August is the week the Hatcher Pass tundra starts to turn
subject.to: Early August is still GREEN at 3,500 ft in the Talkeetnas — fireweed is typically in flower, not gone to seed, and the dwarf birch has not rusted yet. The turn is weeks away

Independence Mine in the tundra turn.fix_why: The evening light window (20:00-22:00 against a 22:15 sunset at azimuth 306) and the fog alternative are both sound, so the shot survives — but the colour was the reason it was scheduled, and that reason is wrong.

subject.from: Qiviut is combed out of the musk oxen during the spring moult
subject.to: NO COMBING SESSION on 9-10 August — the moult, and therefore the combing, runs roughly April to June, so the frame at this stop is the fence-line keeper-and-horns version. Qiviut is taken from the musk oxen during the spring shed

Qiviut, hands and horn.fix_why: The stated primary subject cannot happen on the only night at this stop. The fallback is now the plan rather than the consolation. The farm does not publish combing dates — worth calling. (First attempt tripped the self-reference guard — the replacement repeated the phrase it was replacing, which would have grown the field on every build.)

fix.light: Overcast is the reliable version. The old note claimed a north-east-facing gulch "holds shade well into the morning" — a NE aspect is precisely the one that CATCHES low morning sun, and at the equinox sunrise azimuth here is ~96 degrees. The walls are steep enough that the floor may stay shadowed for a while, but that needs checking on the ground rather than trusting; flat overcast light on wet rock is the version that works whatever the aspect does.

Twin Falls under the first termination d.fix_why: The stated reason inverted how aspect and sun work, so anyone reasoning from it would pick exactly the wrong morning.

Witset Canyon — the fishery, with consen.fix_why: The reference host tourismwitset.com has no DNS record at all — and it was the contact route for the consent step this shot correctly insists on, which makes it the most consequential dead link in the set. Removed rather than replaced with a guess; the permission still has to be sought, now without a starting URL. Coordinate also moved 11 km south-west from a point north-east of the village to Witset itself.

vantage.from: The Highway 16 corridor north of Smithers toward Telkwa
vantage.to: The Highway 16 corridor SOUTH-EAST of Smithers toward Telkwa (Telkwa is ~13 km south-east; going north on 16 heads to Witset, the opposite way)

fix.light: Backlit, and worth shooting that way. Camera faces W and sunset is at azimuth 271 — one degree apart — so the bale lines and barns are rim-lit against the light rather than front-lit. Expose for the sky and let the foreground go graphic.

Bulkley Valley hayfields under a fresh s.fix_why: Sent the traveller the wrong way down the valley on the one scouting afternoon they have, and described front-light the geometry cannot give.

Calico Hills at first light, no reservat.fix_why: Pin was at the fee station by the visitor centre, not the named vantage. Moved to the Calico I overlook. With a 06:00 gate and a 06:50 sunrise the drive up the one-way scenic loop has to be counted.

vantage.append: NOTE: from the SR-159 pull-outs the Red Rock escarpment is BEHIND you, not in the frame — the foreground here is open desert, Joshua and yucca.

The Strip's light dome from the desert.fix_why: SR-159 runs along the eastern base of the escarpment, so looking east at the city glow puts the cliffs behind the camera. Silhouetting them against the dome would need you east of the escarpment — which puts the glow behind you instead. The desert-foreground half of the shot works; the escarpment half cannot.

Sockeye stacking under Russian River Fal.fix_why: Pin was 12.8 km west, out past Jean Lake with no trailhead and no falls. The shot own text said milepost 52 Sterling Highway, which is correct — moved to the Russian River Campground trailhead to match it.

fix.light: Shoot up-lake, W to NW. The old note asked for side light from the north-west while facing SE — but the evening sun here sits at azimuth 280-305, which from a SE-facing camera is directly behind the photographer. That is flat frontal light, the one condition where chop and whitecaps do NOT read as texture. Turning to face W-NW puts the light across and behind the waves, which is what makes them read.

Skilak Lake under wind.fix_why: Facing and light rationale contradicted each other, and the stated combination produces exactly the flat light the shot is trying to avoid.

Bridal Veil Falls, Keystone Canyon, in r.fix_why: Pin was 15.6 km up in the high country above Thompson Pass, past the canyon entirely. Moved to Richardson Highway MP 13-14, which is the 15 minutes from Valdez the shot claims rather than 30-35.

Allison Point — bears, sea lions and the.fix_why: Allison Point sits on the SOUTH shore of Port Valdez — the water, the Solomon Gulch outfall and all the animal action are north to north-west. Facing SW from the Dayville Road pullouts points inland at the mountainside behind you. The predator-prey-and-oil-infrastructure frame needs W-NW.

Cape Blanco taking weather.fix_why: Both numbers were wrong in opposite directions: the pin was 2.1 km inland near the campground, and the trailhead coordinate quoted in the text was 1.64 km offshore in the Pacific. Moved to the lighthouse.

Full moon rising over the eastern canyon.fix_why: The text argues for Lipan Point over the Watchtower, then printed the Watchtower coordinate — navigating to it lands you at the viewpoint the shot just told you not to use. Moved to Lipan Point, 2.85 km west.

The Peter Iredale at dusk.fix_why: Pin was in the Fort Stevens historic-area interior, 4 km NE of the wreck. Moved to the Peter Iredale beach access. The instruction is to park and walk 100 m onto the sand, in the dark, inside a 25-minute post-sunset window.

Cliff Palace with nobody in it.fix_why: Pin fell 1.6 km short of the Cliff Palace Loop entirely. Moved to the Cliff Palace Overlook — for a 200-400mm frame across a canyon from one specific pull-out, the wrong pull-out is the whole shot.

Sawtooths in the still water, Little Red.fix_why: The shot insists on Little Redfish and printed the coordinate for big Redfish, 3.1 km away at the end of the paved road. Moved to Chinook Bay, about 0.4 miles in from ID-75, which is where the shot own cited reference places it.

Stonehenge Memorial on Armistice Day.fix_why: Pin was 0.72 km SSE of the museum, below the highway grade toward the river — wrong side of both the museum and SR-14. This is the departure-day shot with a fixed 11 November window and possibly a timed ceremony.

Catherine Creek arch and the oak savanna.fix_why: Pin was 4.87 km WSW, out in the Columbia River channel — no oak bench, no arch, no parking. Moved to the Old Highway 8 trailhead per WTA.

An angler in the tailwater below the dam.fix_why: Pin was at the dam end of the Little Hole trail, which would have you walking DOWNstream — the opposite of the stated approach, and the facing only makes sense from the real Little Hole trailhead 6 km ENE. Moved there.

Dall sheep and the braided Savage River.fix_why: Pin was in the Nenana River valley south of the park entrance, off the park road entirely. Moved to the Savage River day-use area at Mile 15 — the end of the private-vehicle section, which is what the narrative describes.

Naches Peak Loop — crimson huckleberry a.fix_why: Wrong pass, 28 km off: the pin was White Pass on US-12, copied from the trip POI. Naches Peak starts at Tipsoo Lake on Chinook Pass, a different highway reached via SR-123 and Cayuse Pass. A 5am arrival at the wrong pass loses the alpenglow with no recovery.

Reflection Lakes before the wind.fix_why: Pin was the Ohanapecosh coordinate, reused verbatim from the Silver Falls shot below it — 13.5 km away and an hour apart by road. For a shot that is ten minutes of dead-calm alpenglow on a shoreline, the wrong lake in the dark is a total loss.

Trillium Lake, first snow on Hood.fix_why: Pin was 4.5 km north up toward US-26. Moved to the lake and its dam viewpoint. The whole shot is 20 minutes of alpenglow on a pre-dawn arrival.

light.to: roughly 4:25-4:55pm, straddling the 16:41-16:43 sunset rather than ending before it

Half Dome's last light from Sentinel Bri.fix_why: Two errors. The pin was the Lower Yosemite Fall trailhead, 800 m away on the wrong side of the village — moved to Sentinel Bridge. And the stated 16:10-16:35 window ENDS 6-8 minutes before the sun actually sets on 19-23 Dec (16:41-16:43), when alpenglow on the face peaks at and just after true sunset.

The elbow of the Salmon Glacier from the.fix_why: Facing corrected: from anywhere on Salmon River Road the glacier and its elbow lie north to north-west, so the old S bearing pointed away from the subject. The coordinate is left alone and the flag stays OPEN — the finding could not resolve whether the pin is short of the summit viewpoint or the bearing was simply wrong, and guessing a replacement is how a wrong pin gets made.
The elbow of the Salmon Glacier from the.blocked_why: The finding cannot say whether the pin is short of the summit viewpoint or the bearing is inverted, and gives no replacement coordinate. The bearing half is applied; the pin needs someone who has driven the Salmon River Road.

Bear Glacier and its trimline — a retrea.fix_why: Bear Glacier sits on the SOUTH side of Highway 37A across Strohn Lake — on the left driving west from Meziadin. Facing N turned the camera onto the opposite valley wall, and the trimline-over-ice-front composition only works aimed at the glacier.

Snow above saguaros on the Catalina High.fix_why: The pin was Mount Lemmon Ski Valley, 10.3 km away and ~2,500 ft above the saguaro belt — from there no cactus is visible and the shot cannot be made. The finding does not give a Windy Point coordinate and I will not supply one, so the pin is REMOVED rather than replaced. The vantage text still names Windy Point.

fix.light: Morning. The cirque opens to the north-east — which is why the vantage faces NE down onto Kathleen Lake — so it takes direct sun EARLY and is flat grey by late afternoon. The old note sent you up for an afternoon window on a bowl that is already in shadow by then.

The King's Throne cirque over Kathleen L.fix_why: This stop is one night, 28-29 Aug, and the climb is 4-6 hours. Aiming it at the wrong half of the day did not just cost the light, it cost the only chance at the shot.

fix.light: Sunrise. The Kluane front rises on the WEST side of the Shakwak Trench, so from pullouts east of the village you are looking at an east-facing wall: it takes the first light while the plain is still in shadow. At sunset — azimuth ~297 degrees in late August — that same face goes into shadow first and the plain holds the light, which is the reverse of the two-plane separation this shot is after.

The wall behind Haines Junction.fix_why: Light window inverted. The coordinate is also the townsite rather than the pullout the vantage describes; no replacement was given, so the pin stays and says what it is instead of being moved to a guess. The pin is deliberately left as-is and not annotated in the vantage text: an earlier attempt appended the caveat to a string that still contained the coordinate, so the replacement re-applied on every run and the file never converged.

fix.light: Sunset, not first light. From the visitor centre St Helens bears 103 degrees ESE — and mid-October sunrise azimuth here is 103-104 degrees, so at dawn the sun rises essentially THROUGH the mountain and any long lens is shooting into flare at a dead backlit silhouette. The lit west face over still water is an evening picture: sunset azimuth ~256 degrees puts the light squarely on the flank you can see.

The volcano across Silver Lake at first.fix_why: The entry calls this "the reliable shot at this stop", so the whole stop leaned on a frame that could not be made at the stated hour. Title still says "at first light" — worth renaming when the shot list is next edited.

fix.light: Be on the ridge 30 minutes before sunrise. Facing west from Misery Ridge with the sun coming up behind you, the canyon fog is FRONT-lit — it glows white and holds detail — and the spires warm up at the same time. Backlit fog would need you shooting toward the sun, which is the opposite direction. The picture is real; the old description had the optics backwards and would have had you metering for a glow that never arrives.

Monkey Face over a fog-filled Crooked Ri.fix_why: Internally contradictory: it had the spires already lit at the same moment the sun cleared the rim behind them.

fix.light: Mid-morning to mid-afternoon. Mexican gold poppies CLOSE as light and temperature fall, and on the mesa in early March they are typically shut by mid-to-late afternoon — well before the last hour of daylight (sunset ~18:30 on 2-4 Mar). Any backlit low-sun work has to happen before the flowers fold, not after.

Mexican gold poppies on Peridot Mesa.fix_why: The card recommended the exact hour the subject disappears, then acknowledged the flowers close and did not change the advice. It is a 60-mile drive east from Superior and needs a permit — arriving to shut flowers is the whole cost.

vantage.from: US 60 pullouts east of Superior looking up at the Apache Leap cliff face
vantage.to: from the town side, WEST of and below the escarpment, looking up and east at the cliff face

Apache Leap and the ground underneath it.fix_why: Apache Leap is the west-facing escarpment immediately east of and above Superior. Both the facing: E field and the late-afternoon light note require you to be WEST of it. The stated pullouts put you above and behind the wall inside Queen Creek Canyon — no cliff face to look up at, no town below, no sunset light on the rock.

vantage.from: the south rim of the bowl
vantage.to: the standard viewing rim NORTH-WEST of the arch, shooting south-east

Delicate Arch at last light — and the fr.fix_why: The premise is the La Sals filling the space behind the arch. They bear 145 degrees — south-east — so the frame only exists from north-west of the arch looking SE, which is where the standard rim happens to be. As written it sent you to the south rim facing N, with the range directly behind the camera and out of shot entirely.

Canyon Road, lit windows, no farolitos.fix_why: Sunset on 24-30 Mar is 19:22 and civil twilight ends 19:47, so the stated 18:45-19:20 window ended two minutes BEFORE sunset — direct late daylight with the window lights invisible, which is precisely the failure the shot exists to avoid.

fix.light: Sunrise. The photographed facade of the T.A. Moulton barn faces roughly EAST, toward Mormon Row Road — which is why the standard frame works: you stand east of it and shoot WNW with the sun at your back, the barn front lit warm while the Tetons behind catch alpenglow.

Moulton Barn with the range still white.fix_why: The instruction was right and the stated reason was wrong — it claimed a west-facing facade lit by an eastern sunrise, which cannot happen, and anyone reasoning from it would stand on the wrong side. The pin was also 2.6 km north-east on Antelope Flats Road rather than on Mormon Row.

fix.light: Backlit, and shoot it that way. Camera faces W and sunset is at azimuth 293 — only 23 degrees apart — so the calves are rim-lit against the light, not front-lit. That is a better picture than the card implied: expose for the highlights, let the bodies go dark, and use the low sun through the dust and the fur.

Red dogs on Antelope Flats.fix_why: The card described front-light the geometry cannot give. Rather than move the shot, this describes what is actually there — a rim-lit frame — because backlit red dogs in dust is the stronger image anyway.

subject.from: Late May is graduation and end-of-semester week — the town is at its most itself
subject.to: Late May is the quiet gap — MSU commencement is early-to-mid May, so the students have already gone and the summer season has not started

Main Street closed by the Bridgers.fix_why: The blue-hour geometry was fine; only the human-activity premise was misdated. You arrive to a quieter town than the card promised, which changes what the street scene actually is.

fix.light: Solstice midnight, and treat the moon as a non-factor. Computed illumination on 12-15 June 2027 is 62%, 72%, 81% and 88% — but a waxing gibbous this near the solstice sits at declination around -20 degrees and barely clears the horizon at 58.95N. It will not light the Terminal Range across the lake. What you actually have is the sky itself: the sun only reaches ~7.6 degrees below the horizon at 01:00, so this is all-night nautical twilight — deep blue, never dark.

Solstice midnight blue.fix_why: Planning around moonlight that cannot arrive. The picture is the twilight, not the moon.

fix.light: NOT an aurora window — there is no darkness. Stay is 5-9 Aug 2027 at 62.66N, where the sun's minimum depression at solar midnight is only about -11 degrees: bright nautical twilight all night, no astronomical dark at all. Shoot the twilight over Denali instead, which is genuinely good here. The moon note is also only half right — illumination runs 13.5% on 5 Aug to 43% by the night of 8 Aug.

resolves: SEASON — there is not enough darkness
First aurora of the season over Denali V.fix_why: The stop is named for a shot that is physically impossible on its own dates. The consolation — Denali under all-night twilight — is real and is now what the card describes.

subject.from: January is the tail of the rut
subject.to: January is the START of lambing — Arizona desert bighorn breed roughly July to October, and lambs arrive January to June

Desert bighorn on the skyline.fix_why: It matters operationally, not just factually: in late January you will meet ewes with newborn lambs rather than rutting rams. Different picture, and a higher disturbance risk — the ethical caution was right for the wrong reason.

light.to: any dark evening 25-26 January — you depart on the 27th, and the 26th is the true new moon at 0.0%

resolves: DATE RANGE extends past the stay
New moon over the Kofa Mountains.fix_why: Three of the five offered evenings fall after departure. The 26th is the genuinely dark night and is now the one named.

vantage.to: about twelve miles — a ~24-mile round trip on foot, or a serious bike day

An empty Going-to-the-Sun Road.fix_why: The described subject — the cliff-shelf cut into the Garden Wall with Heavens Peak and Bird Woman Falls across the valley — is roughly 12 miles above the Avalanche Creek closure gate, not the 2-4 the card costed. And a 24-mile day guarantees you are in avalanche terrain in the afternoon, which the shot's own caution says to avoid.

fix.light: Evening, not first light. From Apgar the head of the lake bears ~42 degrees and sunrise on 24 May is at azimuth 57 — shooting NE up-lake at dawn puts the rising sun almost in the frame and the Divide in silhouette. Sunset at 21:22, azimuth 304, front-lights those same peaks with the sun behind your left shoulder, which is the geometry this shot actually describes. Mirror-calm water is just as available in the evening on a still day.

Lake McDonald cobbles at first light.fix_why: Same picture, wrong end of the day — and the title still says "at first light", worth renaming on the next edit.

fix.light: 21:00-22:00, not 23:00. BC Parks gates the Alpha Pool 7am to 22:30 with no admission after 22:00, and the vantage is the boardwalk inside that gate — so the old 22:30-00:30 window sat entirely inside the closure. In mid-June at this latitude the sun is still up and low at 21:00, which is warm light on the swamp anyway. It is the gate that kills the later window, not the light.

Moose in the warm swamp at 23:00.fix_why: The shot was scheduled entirely inside the park's closure. Worth confirming with BC Parks whether the boardwalk, as distinct from the pool, stays open later.

fix.light: Afternoon, and drop the sunset requirement. The shot was built on "pick the day where a minus tide and sunset overlap" — on 19-25 Oct 2027 at La Push no such day exists. The workable frame is the 25 Oct low at 16:07 in flat afternoon light. Chasing the overlap means walking the 1.5 miles back on a flooding tide in the dark, which is the drowning hazard the shot's own caution names.

Hole-in-the-Wall on a first-storm swell.fix_why: The day the shot was built around does not occur during the stay.

fix.light: One usable afternoon: 25 Nov, low of -0.49 ft at 16:23, about 18 minutes before sunset. The old rationale was inverted — it claimed late-November afternoon minus tides against unphotographable pre-dawn summer ones, but of the week only 24 and 25 Nov fall in usable light and only the 25th clears the shot's own "roughly 0.0 ft or lower" bar. Treat it as a single-day shot, not a week of chances.

Cobble Beach on a minus tide.fix_why: Two findings on one shot. The tide window is a quarter of what was claimed. And facing was tagged E while the craft note asks for the lighthouse behind the stones — Yaquina Head Light stands at the far WESTERN tip, so the camera looks west. The coordinate is left alone: the finding says both pins sit north of the tower and the vantage describes ground south and east of it, but gives no replacement, and I will not invent one.

fix.light: Not 18:30 — Orion is below the eastern horizon then, and facing W at that hour gives you Pegasus and Cygnus setting. Orion clears the Sierra crest only in the small hours. New moon falls ~28 Dec so the sky is genuinely dark, but this collides with the 07:04 Mobius Arch dawn on the single night here: one or the other, not both.

Orion over the crest.fix_why: The stated hour pointed the camera at the wrong half of the sky, and fixing it creates a real conflict with the other shot at this stop that the card should state rather than hide.

Mobius Arch, first light on Whitney.blocked_why: The shot has no lat/lng at all and the finding supplies none. It is a one-morning dawn commitment, 45 minutes early in the dark on graded dirt, on a loop the caution says is easy to lose. This needs a real coordinate, not a guess.

fix.light: 05:20-06:00, with the core very low over the range. The galactic centre only crosses altitude zero around 04:55 and needs several more degrees to be worth shooting, so the old 04:15-06:00 window front-loads an hour of nothing. Moon is not a constraint — new moon is ~26 Jan 2028, so every pre-dawn of the 8-night stay through about 3 Feb is moonless.

The core rising before dawn.fix_why: An hour of standing in the cold before the subject is above the horizon.

vantage.from: Stand on the F Street bridge over the Arkansas, mid-span, and shoot north up F Street into town
vantage.to: Stand ON F Street between roughly 1st and 3rd, looking north/NNE toward the bridge

F Street, blue hour, spring runoff not y.fix_why: The historic district is on the SOUTH bank and the bridge sits at its edge — from mid-span you are looking away from the storefronts the shot is about. The NE facing tag was right; the standing position was not.

vantage.from: the US-287 pull-outs west of it, along the north shore
vantage.to: the US-287 pull-outs EAST of the visitor centre, along the lakeshore

Quake Lake's drowned forest.fix_why: Two findings. The visitor centre sits on top of the 1959 slide that dammed the Madison, so the lake and its snags are east of it — the stated pull-outs face the empty side. And the Forest Service reference no longer resolves after their site migration; the caution told you to confirm opening dates through a dead link, so it is removed rather than replaced with a guessed URL.

fix.light: 21:30-23:45, not 23:00-01:30. Whitehorse at 60.72N does NOT have midnight sun — the sun sets around midnight at solstice, so over half the old window has no directional light at all. Note also that with the camera facing N and the late sun near north, you are shooting INTO the light rather than receiving it across the canyon wall.

Miles Canyon at midnight.fix_why: The card promised a sun that has not set, in a place where it sets.

fix.light: Inside opening hours only — 10:00 to 18:00. The Yukon Wildlife Preserve does NOT permit personal vehicles — their own FAQ is explicit — so the "drive the 5 km loop slowly in the truck" instruction and the roadside difficulty are both wrong. It is a walked loop, or the scheduled bus. The preserve also closes at 18:00. The old "evening, from about 20:00" window falls entirely after closing. Walk the loop, or book the 15:00 bus.

Muskox and thinhorn at the preserve.fix_why: Unshootable as written, twice over: the vehicle is not allowed and the hour is after the gate.

fix.light: Morning only, 10:00 opening to about 12:00. The Yukon Wildlife Preserve does NOT permit personal vehicles — their own FAQ is explicit — so the "drive the 5 km loop slowly in the truck" instruction and the roadside difficulty are both wrong. It is a walked loop, or the scheduled bus. The preserve also closes at 18:00. The stated evening half (18:30-20:30) is after closing, so the reachable window is the morning — and it is not the first two hours of light either, since sunrise is ~07:15 and the gate opens at 10:00.

Muskox in September coat.fix_why: Same defect as the June visit to the same preserve.

fix.light: Late night, after moonset. "Best on the nights either side of new moon" is unfollowable on these fixed dates — 8-12 Sept 2027 runs from a 7-day to an 11-day waxing gibbous, 46% to 85% illuminated. The dark window shrinks to the tail of each night and by the last night is essentially gone. Expect a washed sky before moonset and plan the attempts after it.

Aurora over the Yukon River.fix_why: The shot gave advice that cannot be followed on dates that cannot move, without saying so.

fix.light: Start at first light and accept the icefield in mid-morning light. The old "leave the trailhead by 03:30-04:00 to be at the upper viewpoints for first light around 05:00" contradicts the shot's own "allow 6-8 hours" — you cannot climb 3,200 ft in an hour. Going up in the dark also puts you on a brushy trail in bear country before daylight.

Harding Icefield from above the ice.fix_why: The reference 404d because the live NPS page uses underscores rather than hyphens — corrected rather than removed, since the real page exists.

The year markers on Exit Glacier Road.fix_why: Exit Glacier Road runs almost due west and the terminus lies west-to-south-west beyond it, so the NW tag was off by 45-70 degrees. Low consequence for exposure — the shot wants flat overcast — but it misleads anyone pre-checking a sun-position app for the early-morning variant.

light.from: Mid-August gives full dark by around 22:30
light.to: Mid-August sunset here is about 21:35, so 22:30 is barely 55 minutes past it — civil-to-nautical twilight, NOT full dark

Kuskulana Bridge from below the deck.fix_why: Harmless for the pre-sunset frame the shot actually wants, but anyone planning a night or star frame off that sentence would be an hour or more out at 61.5N.

caution.from: Wells Gray park roads and facilities begin shutting down after mid-Sep
caution.to: The Clearwater Valley Road corridor is open YEAR-ROUND, plowed and sanded through winter — late September is not a closure risk. The only real caveat is that some lower-corridor parking areas can be unusable in deep winter. Facilities begin winding down after mid-Sep

Helmcken Falls in autumn low water.fix_why: Both road claims were wrong in the direction that would have made you skip the shot on a four-night stop.

vantage.from: with the jetty and the North Head headland behind
vantage.to: with the North Jetty and the CAPE DISAPPOINTMENT headland and lighthouse behind (North Head is a different headland 3 km away)

fix.light: Backlit, and better for it. Camera faces W and sunset is at azimuth 250 — 20 degrees apart — so spray and storm surf are lit from behind rather than in front. Expose for the highlights and let the wave shapes go to silhouette and translucence.

Waikiki Beach in a Pacific gale.fix_why: Two headlands 3 km apart were conflated, and the pin was 700 m north of the actual parking area — on a gale day with a short window that matters. Light description also had the geometry backwards.

fix.light: Backlit. Camera faces SW and sunset is at azimuth 240 — 15 degrees apart — so the lighthouse and the tidepool foreground are rim-lit against the sun, not front-lit. Expose for the sky, use the wet rock as reflective foreground, and accept the lighthouse as a shape rather than a detailed subject.

Battery Point at a winter low tide.fix_why: The card described front-light that the geometry cannot deliver at that hour.

caution.append: NOT AVAILABLE on the first day at least: NPS opens the East Entrance Road over Sylvan Pass and the Canyon-to-Lake section on the first Friday in May, and arrival is Thursday 6 May 2027. Lake Butte Overlook is beyond that gate.

Breaking ice on Yellowstone Lake.fix_why: The opening claim came from a stale non-authoritative source and does not survive the actual arrival date.

vantage.append: NOTE: shoot from the Emerald Bay shoreline in the townsite, not the hotel car park — the old pin was the hotel itself, and Vimy Peak bears ESE from Emerald Bay.

Prince of Wales on its knoll, dawn.fix_why: The vantage rejected the hotel car park and then gave the hotel's own coordinate with a NE facing. Vimy Peak — whose lighting the craft note uses as the trigger — bears 121 degrees ESE from Emerald Bay, 145 degrees away from the stated bearing and impossible to hold in the same 24-70mm frame.

subject.to: Nearly ten years on (the Kenow fire burned September 2017; this stay is May 2027)

The Kenow burn on the Red Rock Parkway.fix_why: Not pedantry — it changes the picture. By year ten a significant fraction of the standing snags in Blakiston Valley will have fallen and the understory is well advanced, which undercuts the "rank on rank of repeating black verticals" that the 70-200mm compression depends on.

fix.light: Full darkness arrives about two hours later than the card said — on 3 September at Dawson, sunset is 21:25, civil twilight ends 22:17 and nautical twilight runs later still, so "true darkness around 23:30" understates it. Face NORTH: the aurora sits north from Dawson, and the old W-facing frame points at the town and the Yukon confluence, which only works during a strong overhead substorm.

Aurora over the Yukon from Midnight Dome.fix_why: Wrong by roughly two hours on when to be up there, and pointed at the wrong quarter of the sky.

vantage.from: looking upstream and across at the mill stacks
vantage.to: looking DOWNSTREAM and across at the mill stacks

Mill steam at first light.fix_why: The facing tag was right and the word "upstream" was wrong — the pulp mill bears 67 degrees ENE from Cottonwood Island, which is downstream. As written the two directions sent you to opposite ends of the park in the dark.

_fix: Applies a review finding to the shot itself. `fix` maps a field to either a replacement string, or {from, to} for a substring swap; `resolves` lists a phrase from the flag text, and any flag containing it is re-labelled src='fixed' so the card reads 'corrections applied' instead of 'problems found'. Fixes run BEFORE tags are derived — the derivation reads the light text, so correcting a time after tagging would leave the tags wrong.
_blocked: blocked:true marks a finding that cannot be applied without information nobody has published — usually a replacement coordinate. It counts toward `prog` in progress.py but never toward `have`, because closing it would mean inventing the number.
_append: fix: {field: {append: 'text'}} adds a note to the end of a field, once. Use it for annotations — writing them as {from: X, to: X + note} is self-referential and grows the field on every build.
